'''''Tordylium maximum''''', known as '''hartwort''', is an annual or biennial [[flowering plant]] in the carrot family ([[Apiaceae]]).<ref name=Stac10p828/>

==Description==

''Tordylium maximum'' is a hairy or bristly [[Biennial plant|biennial]] or [[Annual plant|annual]], growing to about {{convert|30|–|130|cm|ft|abbr=on|1}} tall, with a hollow ridged stem that is usually branched. The lower leaves are [[Pinnation|pinnate]], with two to five pairs of coarsely toothed leaflets. The upper leaves may be reduced to a single leaflet. The flowers are arranged in flat [[umbel]]s, with 5–15 rays. Like other members of the genus ''[[Tordylium]]'', the flowers are white, with the outer flowers having some much longer petals on the outer side of the umbel. The fruits are {{convert|5|–|8|mm|in|abbr=on|2}} long.<ref name=Tuti68/><ref name=Stac10p828/>

==Taxonomy==

''Tordylium maximum'' was first described by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753 in ''[[Species Plantarum]]''.<ref name=IPNI_Tordylium_maximum/><ref name=Linn53/>

==Distribution==

''Tordylium maximum'' is a species of south and south central Europe, probably not native in the northern parts of its range.<ref name=Tuti68/> It has been found in south-east [[England]], but only in one location in south [[Essex]] since 1875.<ref name=Stac10p828/>
